notes.text: Your pawn stops Black's bishop from pinning the knight that holds d4.
You take back with the pawn, keeping two centre pawns and hitting the bishop again.
Your knight dodges the e4 pawn and attacks both that pawn and the e6 bishop.
Your bishop steps back from the pawn but keeps watching the knight that guards e5.
Your pawn takes and now attacks the knight that your bishop pins to the king.
Trading bishops pulls Black's queen off its path to g5, so e5 can be taken.
Your bishop escapes the pawn and takes the diagonal Black's f-pawn left open.
Your king gets safe, and the rook can go to e1 behind the e4 pawn.
Your second rook comes to the centre and backs up the e5 pawn.
Taking the knight removes the e5 pawn's only defender, so you can win your pawn back.
Your pawn backs up d4 and gives your bishop a retreat square on c2.
Your knight guards the e4 pawn and starts its trip toward g3.
You win the pawn back, and your new e5 pawn attacks Black's knight.
Your rook backs up the queen on the e-file, piling onto Black's knight on e4.
Taking on b5 opens the a-file for your rook while Black's pieces sit on the kingside.
Your bishop attacks the undefended knight on c6, with the a8 rook behind it.
Your bishop escapes the b5 pawn and guards your e4 pawn from c2.
Your pawn challenges e5 a second time and frees your dark bishop.
Trading queens forces Black's king to recapture, so it can never castle.
The check makes Black block with a piece before your rook checks on the e-file.
Your bishop escapes the c6 pawn while staying on the diagonal toward Black's king.
Your knight takes the pawn back and sits in the centre, guarded by the queen.
Black's strong knight goes, and retaking with the d-pawn will open the d-file.
Taking opens the e-file, where your rook can soon check Black's uncastled king.
Taking on d4 with your queen lets Black's pawns trap your bishop, so you offer a pawn.
Your pawn keeps Black's bishop off g4, where it would pin the knight guarding d4.
Your knight hits the queen and the c7 pawn, so Black has no time to take your bishop.
You trade off the knight hitting your bishop; once Black recaptures, your e-pawn can chase its other knight.
Your bishop attacks the unguarded knight on a5, so Black must trade it off now.
Your pawn chases the c6 knight away and shuts the b7 bishop's diagonal.
Your d-pawn joins the knight against e5 and opens a path for your dark bishop.
Your king gets safe first, so you can open the centre with your d-pawn next.
You take the pawn back, and your knight joins the bishop against Black's pinned knight.
Your queen completes the trade, and now three of your pieces bear down on the e5 pawn.
You take the e5 pawn and your new pawn hits Black's knight on f6.
Your knight develops with an eye on d5, where it would hit Black's queen.
Your queen attacks the unprotected knight on e4 and makes it retreat.
You win the knight back; once Black's pawn retakes, offer the c-pawn instead of using your queen.
Your rook takes the loose knight, and your king still attacks the bishop on h2.
You take the knight back, and your queen stands ready to recapture on d4.
Your pawn props up e4 and opens the diagonal for your dark bishop.
Your pawn hits e5 and opens your bishop's line to the loose g5 pawn.
Your queen steps out of the bishop's attack and can drop back to f1 to challenge Black's queen.
Castling guards g2 with your king, so now you really threaten to take on e5.
You strike at the e5 pawn to open the centre while Black's king is still there.
You give your rook for Black's knight and the bishop that takes back, since your queen recaptures.
Your bishop steps away from the pawn's attack and now points at f7.
Your queen grabs the pawn; if Black trades queens, a discovered check wins the queen back.
Your bishop takes the diagonal Black's f-pawn just opened and stops Black from castling.
Your bishop forks both knights, and Black cannot save them both.
Your pawn hits e5 a second time and opens the line for your dark bishop.
Your second knight backs up f3, so you can recapture there with a knight.
You remove Black's only developed piece, and its e-pawn gets pulled away from the centre.
Your pawn hits the bishop on c5 and the e5 pawn, so Black must react.
Your attacked knight escapes by taking the e5 pawn and lands in the centre.
Your queen takes back and attacks the corner rook along the diagonal the g-pawn left open.
Your pawn backs up e4 and opens your bishop's path toward g5.
You take the pawn Black offered, and it has no way to recapture yet.
Your knight wins the pawn back and takes a central post, guarded by your queen.
Your pawn hits e5 a second time, opening the centre before Black's bishop reaches g7.
Leave the bishop alone: taking it opens the h-file toward your king, so support e4 instead.
Now the pawn is safe to take, and your knight hits Black's queen too.
Your rook takes the d-file, the only fully open file on the board.
Your c-pawn props up d5 against Black's c6 pawn and hits b5.
You take the knight back; next your rook comes to e1 against Black's stranded knight.
Your knight recaptures and joins the bishop against Black's pinned knight on c6.
Your pawn joins the knight in attacking e5, pushing Black to trade its e-pawn.
Retaking with the a-pawn opens the a-file, and your rook now attacks the a6 pawn.
Your bishop steps back to aim at f7 before Black's c-pawn can chase it.
Your queen hits the loose knight on e4 and the pinned knight on c6 together.
You remove the knight that guards e5, so your knight can take that pawn.
Your pawn hits the queen and shuts its path to f2.
Your bishop guards f2, so the queen's second try also comes to nothing.
You hit the e5 pawn a second time before Black has finished developing.
Black could only save one knight, so your bishop takes the other.
Black's knight took a pawn you had defended, so recapturing wins a piece for a pawn.
Your f-pawn grabs kingside space and gives your rook a file to work behind.
Your c-pawn backs up d4, so you can retake there with a pawn and keep your centre.
Your pawn attacks the bishop on g4, so Black has to decide what to do with it.
Black's pin on your knight weakens d4, so your bishop adds a defender.
You trade off the knight guarding e5, so your knight can take that pawn next.
Your bishop drops back still eyeing the loosened h6 pawn, ready for your queen behind it.
Your queen recaptures in the centre, and your bishop can pin a knight that chases it.
Your b-pawn grabs queenside space and clears b2 for your bishop to hit the d4 pawn.
Your knight develops toward the centre while Black's knight is stuck on b7.
Your knight takes the e5 pawn that just lost its only defender.
Your knight attacks the bishop on e6, aiming to trade off one of Black's two bishops.
You must take the knight back, though Black's e-pawn will recapture yours.
Your bishop pins the f6 knight to Black's queen and tempts the h-pawn forward.
Black's b-pawn had no protection, so your bishop simply takes it for free.
You prepare to build a pawn centre with d4 and let Black take on e4.
Your king gets safe, and the rook can step to e1 to back the e4 pawn.
Your pawn challenges the e5 pawn at once and opens the diagonal for your dark bishop.
Your bishop is attacked, so it sells itself for a pawn and opens up Black's king.
Your queen guards e4 and eyes c4, hitting Black's bishop and its castling square.
Your bishop develops and supports the d4 pawn that Black's c-pawn just attacked.
Your knight takes back the pawn you gave up, backed by the rook on e1.
Your king gets safe and guards g2 before Black's queen can jump out to g5.
You take the pawn back and add a second attacker on Black's pinned knight.
Your bishop steps back but keeps the knight pinned while your d-pawn attacks it.
Your knight develops and backs up the e4 pawn Black is aiming at.
Your rook attacks the loose knight on e4, on the same file as Black's king.
You win your pawn back and attack Black's knight, which must move again.
The pawn backs up d5 against Black's knight and leaves c3 free for your knight.
Your knight collects the e5 pawn that lost its only defender.
Your rook backs up the e4 pawn so your d-pawn can advance to d4 next.
Your bishop pins the knight to Black's king, so your queen stays in the centre.
You take the knight back; after Black's pawn recaptures, push your c-pawn instead of retaking with the queen.
Your rook checks down the open file, so Black must block with a kingside piece.
Your bishop steps away from the pawn and now looks straight at f7.
Taking removes the pawn that hit your bishop and leaves e5 loose for your knight.
Your rook guards the e4 pawn Black's knight just attacked and lines up against the king.
Castling also frees your rook to come to e1 behind the e4 pawn.
Your knight wins the pawn back and joins the bishop against the pinned c6 knight.
Your queen attacks the unguarded knight on e4, so Black must defend or move it.
Your bishop develops and covers f2, the pawn Black's queen was aiming at.
You take the queen back with check from your bishop, and the h2 bishop falls next.
Your c-pawn backs up d4 and opens c2 as a retreat for your bishop.
Your knight develops by attacking Black's queen, which must spend another move running away.
Your pawn takes the centre with c3 behind it and hits Black's bishop.
Your bishop dodges the c6 pawn and takes aim at the f7 pawn.
Your bishop backs up the e4 pawn, so your knight is free to head for f1.
Your knight heads for g3 on the kingside and unblocks your c1 bishop.
Your queen and rook now both hit the knight on e4, and the queen guards d4.
Your knight steps aside to uncover the bishop's check while hitting Black's queen on d5.
Your bishop steps away from the c6 pawn to a square where Black's d5 push won't hit it.
Your bishop drops back to guard e4, out of reach of Black's knight coming to a5.
Your bishop steps out of reach of a c-pawn kick and keeps its line toward Black's king.
Your king gets safe first, so you can open the centre with your d-pawn next.
Your pawn steps past the f5 pawn and takes f6 away from Black's knight.
Your queen takes back and aims straight at the undefended g7 pawn.
Your c-pawn backs up the d4 push, which will hit Black's bishop and e5 pawn.
With c3 backing it, your d-pawn takes the centre and challenges the e5 pawn.
Your rook retakes onto the open d-file while your bishop keeps guarding the knight.
Your c-pawn prepares d4, building a centre while hitting Black's bishop.
Your bishop escapes the d5 pawn with check, so you lose no time retreating.
Your knight takes the piece back and keeps your queenside pawns in one unbroken row.
You strike at e5 to open the centre while Black's knight sits on the edge.
Taking back with the pawn keeps your centre whole and frees c3 for your knight.
Your rook defends the e4 pawn, which Black's knight and bishop are both eyeing.
Your bishop forks both black knights, and neither one is defended.
Your rook hits the d5 bishop while your king attacks the other, so one falls.
Your king gets safe, and the rook can come to e1 facing Black's uncastled king.
You win the queen back, and Black's knight and bishop are both under attack.
Your pawn takes the knight, and Black only gets a pawn back for it.
Your knight uncovers check from the bishop and attacks the queen, winning it back.
Your rook guards the e4 pawn and lines up with Black's queen down the file.
You trade off the knight that was hitting both your bishop and your f3 knight.
Taking the knight removes the e5 pawn's only defender, so you can win your pawn back.
Your king gets safe and your rook is free to face Black's queen from e1.
Your bishop sidesteps the a-pawn and takes aim at the f7 pawn.
Your last piece comes out and guards f3, where Black's bishop wanted to land.
Your king gets safe before the centre opens, and the rook can come to e1.
Your rook attacks the unprotected knight on e4 and makes it retreat.
Your king takes the stray bishop, leaving two minor pieces for Black's rook and two pawns.
Your pawn takes on e5, leaving you a pawn ahead with your queen hitting d5.
Trading off the c5 knight removes the guard of e4, where your bishop wants to go.
Your attacked knight steps back to hit the d4 pawn, heading for g3 or f4.
Your knight develops by attacking Black's queen, which must move again.
This pawn prepares the c4 push, which will support your d5 pawn.
Your king gets safe, and your rook can now come to the e-file against the e5 pawn.
You swap off the bishop that your own e4 and d5 pawns would block.
Your knight steps back to guard f2 and hits Black's loose bishop on c5.
Your bishop develops, guards the d4 pawn and clears the way for your knight to d2.
Castling tucks your king away, and your rook now guards f2 against Black's queen.
